name: Feedyio
summary: Shopify product-feed engine (by happyapps.cz) that generates and syncs feeds for Google, Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Bing and 130-plus marketplaces and price-comparison sites, with strong coverage of the Central European channels (Heureka, Glami, Kaufland, Favi). Custom XML, CSV, TXT or JSON feeds are built from your own Liquid template, with category mapping, attribute rules and validation before products get rejected. Launched May 2022.
best_for: Shopify merchants who need several feeds at once, in formats they control — custom XML, CSV, TXT or JSON built from their own template — and especially those selling into Central and Eastern European marketplaces and price-comparison sites, with a catalogue that fits inside a published tier
skip_if: you need one Google Shopping feed and nothing else, where the older and far more widely reviewed feed apps cover the same ground; or your catalogue runs past 65,000 products, which is where the published ladder ends
honest_knock: Two gates decide your bill and neither is about how much value the feeds create. The first is catalogue size: the ladder counts products and variants, and it runs further than the Shopify listing suggests — the listing stops at Pro ($29.99, 6,000 products) and says additional plans are available, while the vendor's own pricing page publishes five more tiers up to $119.99 for 65,000 products. The second is freshness: the free tier updates products once a day and hourly updates start at $9.99, which matters when stock moves faster than a day. Multi-market and multi-language feeds only appear at $19.99. The app is also younger and smaller than the shelf leaders: launched 16 May 2022 by happyapps.cz in Prague, with 115 reviews against thousands for the established Google Shopping feed apps. And the standout integrations — Heureka, Zboží.cz, Árukereső, Glami, Favi, Kaufland — are Central and Eastern European channels; that is the app's real edge, but it is not an edge if you only sell through Google and Meta.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/product-feed-10 and feedyio.com/pricing) Nine published tiers, billed in USD every 30 days through Shopify. The Shopify listing shows only the first four. Free is permanent and covers up to 30 products or 100 variants, one feed, the primary market only, a daily product update and email support. Basic at $9.99 a month raises that to 1,000 products or 2,000 variants, up to five feeds, hourly product updates and the named comparison-shopping integrations (Heureka, Favi and similar), still on the primary market and language only. Advanced at $19.99 covers 2,500 products or 5,000 variants, up to ten feeds, and all markets and languages. Pro at $29.99 covers 6,000 products or 12,000 variants and up to 30 feeds. The listing stops there and says additional plans are available; the vendor's own pricing page prices them: Enterprise $39.99 (10,000 products / 20,000 variants / 40 feeds), Enterprise Plus $59.99 (20,000 / 40,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 2 $89.99 (30,000 / 60,000 / 40), Enterprise Plus 3 $99.99 (50,000 / 100,000 / 40) and Enterprise Plus 4 $119.99 (65,000 / 130,000 / 40). Every paid tier has a 7-day free trial. One inconsistency on that page: the line under the table says every paid plan unlocks Shopify markets, translations and inventory levels, while the Basic card above it lists the primary market and primary language only — the Shopify listing agrees with the card, so confirm before buying Basic for a second market.

compare_with.name: Simprosys Google Shopping Feed, Koongo: Sell on Marketplaces
compare_with.why: the difference is breadth of channel against depth of track record. Simprosys is the shelf leader for the Google, Microsoft, Meta and Pinterest set and carries thousands of reviews (read 10 September 2026 on the Shopify App Store); Feedyio carries 115 and is three years old. What Feedyio has instead is the template editor — you write your own XML, CSV, TXT or JSON in Liquid rather than picking from a fixed list — and a preconfigured set of European comparison and marketplace channels that the Google-first apps treat as an afterthought. If your channels are Google and Meta, buy on track record. If your channels include Heureka, Glami, Kaufland or a marketplace that wants a feed shaped its own way, Feedyio is the one built for that, and the free tier lets you check the output shape before paying.
